question.:question/worked-solution:
Let's set $u=\ln\left(\left(\frac{x}{5}\right)\right).$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x}\,⟹\,1\,\text{d}u=\frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Calculating the limits for $u$ gives the following:

| $x$ | $5 e$ | $5 e^{4}$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $1$ | $4$ |

We now substitute and evaluate as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{25}\int_{5 e}^{5 e^{4}}\frac{5\operatorname{ln}\left(\frac{x}{5}\right)}{4\left(\frac{x}{5}\right)}\,\text{d}x \\ & =\frac{1}{10}\int_{5 e}^{5 e^{4}}\operatorname{ln}\left(\frac{x}{5}\right)\cdot \frac{1}{\left(\frac{x}{5}\right)}\,\text{d}x \\ & =\frac{1}{2}\int_{1}^{4}u\,\text{d}u \\ & =\frac{2}{5}\cdot\left(\frac{5}{4}\cdot \frac{{u}^{2}}{2}\right)|_{1}^{4} \\ & =\frac{2}{5}\cdot\left(\frac{5}{8}\cdot {u}^{2}\right)|_{1}^{4} \\ & =\frac{2}{5}\cdot\left(\frac{5}{8}({4}^{2}-{1}^{2})\right) \\ & =\frac{2}{5}\cdot\left(\frac{5}{8}\cdot 15\right) \\ & =\frac{2}{5}\cdot\left(\frac{75}{8}\right)\end{aligned}
$$
